purpose: Compare required muscle-tendon tension and mechanical power for an athlete-inspired heavy squat and reported box jump. Not a reconstruction of measured individual muscle forces.
athlete_reference_interpretation: Use the athlete's active-career or near-active-career physical capacity as the reference level. The user does not require the squat and jump records to have been filmed on the same date. Do not treat post-retirement Physical: 100 as the principal physical-condition reference.

subject.name: Yun Sung-bin
subject.muscle_architecture: Generic model architecture; individual cross-sections, tendon properties and recruitment are not measured.
subject.morphology_policy: Native 178 cm rigid geometry; segment masses normalized to 87 kg; nonhelper inertias follow validated uniform height similarity. Individual anatomy is unmeasured.

squat.timing_source: User's approximate 1RM scenario assumption, not extracted from performance footage.

box_jump.height_source: User-supplied reported performance, also described in contemporary 2018 reporting.

sequence: Set explicit subject, preparation motion and propulsion assumptions; generate a small-forward jump without a prescribed target box.
Compute and audit ground forces and takeoff state; compute conservative free flight with no box or other support wrench in the air.
Track whole-body COM, both foot soles and the complete foot swept geometry. Airborne joint motion must preserve whole-body angular momentum.
Place a candidate box under an attainable part of the foot path, usually near its high region, with clearance margin; detect top-surface contact from above.
Check the front edge and side faces against the approach path, both feet against the top footprint, and the contact time independently of the COM apex.
Develop and validate impact, deceleration and supported stabilization as a separate subsequent stage.
revised_box_development_method.reported_160cm_usage: A later feasibility comparison target, not an imposed airborne COM rise, takeoff speed or power.
do_not_prescribe_in_free_flight: Independent world-frame foot position and orientation targets that override conservative whole-body dynamics
An external wrench to pull the feet onto the box
A pelvis orientation target that silently changes whole-body angular momentum
revised_box_development_method.power_comparison_window: Ground propulsion before takeoff can be analyzed separately from the unresolved landing phase, once that ground/flight trajectory passes its own audit.
revised_box_development_method.capacity_interpretation: No maximum jump height is inferred automatically from a 240kg squat. Propulsion timing, motion or takeoff-state information must remain explicit inputs or measured references.
revised_box_development_method.implementation_status: Contact-acceleration QP ground dynamics, unilateral support modes and conservative centroidal flight implemented. Generic forward-jump trials pass 14 audits; complete box arrival and landing remain unresolved.

remaining_before_landing: Feet reaching the top surface with plausible whole-body posture
Consistent ballistic COM and conserved angular momentum in free flight
remaining_at_landing: Impact and deceleration without velocity resets or invented supports
existing_box_pipeline_audit.correction: The unresolved work is not limited to landing; previous pre-impact box trials also failed geometry or dynamics checks.

comparison_metrics: Peak and mean scalar muscle-group tension, N, mean per side
Muscle tension-time integral over one physical movement, N s
Vertical combined-system COM pseudo-power, F_ground_z * v_system_COM_z, W; body plus bar for squat
Segmental mechanical-energy rate and joint mechanical power, W, reported separately from COM pseudo-power
GRF, takeoff velocity and COM rise as external-mechanics checks
release_requirements: Reported box height is not substituted for airborne COM rise or converted directly into power.
Squat timing assumptions remain visibly distinct from measured video timing.
The 240kg case must be recomputed using its own trajectory and bar inertia; do not scale existing 100kg tension results.
Retain explicit body-mass, depth, speed, contact and force-sharing assumptions.
No force clipping to preferred magnitudes, no strength ceiling and no invented flight contact or root support wrench.
Rejected box motion does not receive released power or muscle-force results.
Individual muscle-force accuracy is not inferred from numerical equilibrium checks.
execution_note: 240 kg squat and generic forward-jump diagnostics calculated. Reported 160 cm remains an unverified comparison target; no athlete muscle-force result or successful 160 cm jump is claimed.
